instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F. Rub the inside of a 2 1/2-quart baking dish with the oil.
Put the stuffing mix in a bowl and stir in the hot water the box calls for. Set it aside for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, pull the meat off the rotisserie chicken and discard the skin and bones. Chop the meat. That should be about 2 cups.
Put 3 cups of the frozen vegetables in a colander and run hot water over them until they're thawed. Drain them well.
In the baking dish, stir together the vegetables, chicken, soup, 1/3 cup sour cream, 1/2 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp pepper.
Spread the stuffing evenly over the top.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes, until the edges are bubbling and the top is golden.
Serve it hot, spooned straight from the dish. Leftovers keep in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 4 days, or in the freezer for up to 3 months.
method_notes: Spend With Pennies (4.94 from 424 ratings) leads: cooked chicken, thawed mixed vegetables, cream of chicken soup and a little sour cream under a layer of prepared stuffing, baked at 400°F. Cooked chicken is used straight from a rotisserie bird, so the honest time is 45 minutes. Other versions (Taste of Home style, Amanda's Cookin') add more soup or broth or use raw chicken under the stuffing; this follows the lead. It isn't dairy-free or gluten-free, only nut-free as asked.
